question:
Real numbers \(x,\) \(y,\) and \(z\) satisfy the inequalities \(0 < x < 1,\) \(-1 < y < 0,\) and \(1 < z < 2.\)

Which of the following numbers is necessarily positive?
solution:
The lower bounds on \(y\) and \(z\) add to zero. Since \(y>-1\) and \(z>1\), adding gives
\[
y+z>-1+1=0.
\]
Thus choice E is always positive.

For completeness, the other four choices can all be negative at the same allowed values. Take \(x=\frac18\), \(y=-\frac14\), and \(z=\frac32\). Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
y+x^2&=-\frac14+\frac1{64}=-\frac{15}{64},\\
y+xz&=-\frac14+\frac3{16}=-\frac1{16},\\
y+y^2&=-\frac14+\frac1{16}=-\frac3{16},\\
y+2y^2&=-\frac14+\frac2{16}=-\frac18.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore the necessarily positive expression is \(\boxed{y+z}\), choice \(\text{E}\).
